Info-LivePreview: The live summary preview may be wrong, if you are not sure if the preview is correct, use the "Show preview" button.
Header-Exp-Note: Note: Using these experimental features might be unstable and could break the editor or it may not work.
Settings-SameSelection: Highlight same code parts as selected text
Settings-MatchingBracket-Info: Highlights the corresponding opening or closing bracket when you select a bracket character (, {, or [.
Settings-HTMLTags-Info: Colors any tag that is supported by the wiki, for example: "<div>"
Settings-MwFunctions: Stylized template parser functions and parameters
Settings-ReplaceLinksWTemp: Replace links with their custom templates
Settings-ReplaceTempWLinks: Replace link templates with actual links
Exp-StringsCounter: Get a list of all languages and the count
Exp-InvalidTag-Info: Note that it does not check if a function like {{#if:...}} uses only html elements, it will show one as an invalid.
Exp-ShowLiveSummary-Info: Shows a preview summary that updates every 400ms when typing in the summary box. (Requires restart)
Exp-TemplatePageTab: Open a new tab with template name
Exp-TemplatePageTab-Info: While holding CTRL and double clicking on the template name, it opens a new tab to the templates documentation, if the template has spaces, it will open it with spaces.
Panel-UDT-Info: Color - The main color for the template.
Enable background - If set to true, you can add a background, it also adds a small transparency to it. 0% is fully transparent, and 100% is fully opaque.
Name - The name of the template, using the + you can add any templates that are a redirect to the template or are similar to the template. The max is $1
Params - (Optional) The params for the template, if a template has a "MyParam" then it is going to color it in a specific color. The max is $2.
If it doesn't have a parameter, but has "1" then its going to color 1= or {{{1}}} in that color, using the + you can add more parameters.
To import UDT (User Defined Template), you need to convert the templates.js (from the old version of the extension), to a .json file.

Todo so, firstly remove comments, check for any unwanted commas, optionally include only the "TEMPLATES", and change the file extension to .json, then click the up arrow to import UDT. Please note that the import won't detect if the if the template name is correct.
Click on the down arrow to save the file on your desktop, this isn't required, but its recommended if the extension gets an error and fails to save the data.
